text:
Winnipeg put 18 shots on goal in Boston and won 4-2. That sounds like a heist, and it is not quite one. The Bruins out-attempted the Jets 51 to 35, but Winnipeg's looks were better: 3.51 expected goals to 2.52 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and a 52% share of the replays of every shot. Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press called it "a tidy defensive effort," which is about right for a team that gave Boston volume and very little else after the first period.

Kyle Connor was at the center of it, with a goal 65 seconds in and two assists. Morgan Geekie tied it on a Boston power play, and Josh Morrissey restored the lead with a slap shot late in the first on a 6% chance. Fraser Minten tipped in a Mason Lohrei shot to tie it 2-2 midway through the second, and then the game turned on a fourth-line goal. Morgan Barron's backhand at 17:53, from Mario Ferraro and Dawson Mercer, moved Winnipeg from 48% to 71% to win and was the most valuable goal of the night. The Jets out-chanced Boston 1.44 to 0.52 in the third, and Mark Scheifele, fresh off becoming the franchise's all-time leading goal scorer, closed it at 18:48.

Nico Daws stopped 21 of 23 for Winnipeg, a little better than expected. Jeremy Swayman faced only 17 shots and allowed three, though his stop on a 33% chance from Adam Lowry in the second kept it level for a while.

For Boston, the context is not good. Ty Anderson noted the Bruins have dropped four of five at home for the first time since December 2016, and Pavel Zacha's name keeps coming up in trade talk after the Dylan Larkin deal. The Bruins won the October meeting in overtime. This one, they had the puck and Winnipeg had the game.
headline: Jets win with 18 shots, and the Bruins' home slide goes on
